 Advice from the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO)
 
-The IND can ask the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (in Dutch: Rijksdienst voor Ondernemend Nederland or RVO) for advice on the continuity and solvency of businesses. For start-up businesses the RVO uses a point system to assess this. A maximum of 100 points can be obtained. You need at least 50 points for positive advice.
+The IND can ask the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (in Dutch: Rijksdienst voor Ondernemend Nederland or RVO) for advice on the continuity and solvency of businesses. For start-up businesses the RVO uses a point system to assess this. A maximum of 100 points can be obtained. You need at least 65 points for positive advice.

 Last update: 9 April 2026
 
-You have a residence permit as a researcher in a different EU country under Directive (EU) 2016/801. You are coming for a maximum of 180 days out of a 360-day period to carry out research in the Netherlands. Find out what the requirements are and what the process is.
+You have a residence permit as a researcher in a different EU country under Directive (EU) 2016/801. You are coming for a maximum of 120 days out of a 360-day period to carry out research in the Netherlands. Find out what the requirements are and what the process is.
 
 What is short-term mobility?
 
@@ -24,9 +24,9 @@
 
 There are 2 forms of intra-EU mobility for researchers.
 
-Short-term mobility: the researcher comes to the Netherlands to carry out research for a maximum of 180 days out of a 360-day period. No residence permit is required for short-term mobility. Your residence permit in the other country is also valid in the Netherlands.
+Short-term mobility: the researcher comes to the Netherlands to carry out research for a maximum of 120 days out of a 360-day period. No residence permit is required for short-term mobility. Your residence permit in the other country is also valid in the Netherlands.
 
-Long-term mobility: the researcher will come to carry out research in the Netherlands for more than 180 days. A residence permit is required for long-term mobility. Find out more on the web page Residence permit researcher (Directive (EU) 2016/801).
+Long-term mobility: the researcher will come to carry out research in the Netherlands for more than 120 days. A residence permit is required for long-term mobility. Find out more on the web page Residence permit researcher (Directive (EU) 2016/801).
 
 Family members of researchers

 You are going to carry out research at a research institution in the Netherlands. This research institution is recognised by the IND as sponsor. A recognised sponsor is listed in the Public Register Recognised Sponsors.
